correctness.rationale: The constant function has norm one and M_phi 1=phi. Thus the nonconstant coefficients have weighted squared norm at most one. The degree-n sum of |x^alpha|^2/w_alpha is ||x||^(2n), also for countably many coordinates by monotone finite-coordinate truncation, so weighted Cauchy–Schwarz gives absolute convergence and the claimed inner ball. For a unit direction v, multiplication by its linear coordinate is contractive: the Drury–Arveson coordinate row is contractive, as the kernel identity for I-sum_j M_zj M_zj* leaves the constant kernel (finite partial sums are positive, with limiting sum in the countable case). The one-variable contraction calculus for s(r-s)/(1-rs) is justified by uniform Taylor convergence on the closed disk since r=1/sqrt(2). Its degree-n coefficients have absolute value r^n, including degree one. Choosing the coordinate along x realizes the homogeneous absolute sums (r||x||)^n and proves the sharp obstruction beyond r and attainment everywhere on the sphere. On the sphere the profile b has weighted norm one and weighted inner product with |c| equal to the majorant; expanding |||c|-b||_w^2 gives the exact identity. Both terms are nonnegative, and matching moduli is sufficient as well as necessary. No assertion about all phases is needed.
